aggressive_definition_excerpt: We obtained the following novel findings: high-level organ meat intake was an independent predictor for increased aggressive PCa risk; supplementary iron, copper and magnesium increased benign PCa risk; and the AA diet was "healthy" in terms of the relatively lower protein and fat levels and was "unhealthy" in that it more commonly contained organ meat.
grading_caveat: The abstract explicitly labels the endpoint as "aggressive PCa" but provides no operational stage, grade, or risk-group definition.
reason: The abstract analyzes prostate cancer generally and explicitly reports an aggressive incident-risk association for organ meat. The included nutrients are discussed only in relation to general or benign prostate cancer.

exposures.supporting_excerpt: We confirmed previous studies showing that (1) high protein and saturated fat levels in diet were related to increased PCa risk, (2) high-level supplementary selenium intake was harmful rather than beneficial for preventing PCa, and (3) supplementary vitamin B6 was beneficial for preventing benign PCa.
exposures.reason: Selenium is associated only with general PCa in the abstract; the aggressive finding concerns organ meat.
